purpose: Pitavastatin is used to lower bad cholesterol (LDL) and triglycerides in your blood, while helping to raise your good cholesterol (HDL). It is prescribed to reduce your risk of heart disease and stroke. It works best when combined with a heart-healthy diet and regular exercise.
how_it_works: Your liver naturally makes cholesterol, and pitavastatin works by blocking a key enzyme in the liver called HMG-CoA reductase that is responsible for producing it. By slowing down cholesterol production, your liver then pulls more bad cholesterol out of your bloodstream to compensate. The result is lower cholesterol levels circulating in your blood.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include muscle aches or weakness, joint pain, headache, and digestive issues like constipation or nausea. Most people tolerate this medication very well. Let your doctor know if you notice any unusual or severe muscle pain, as this can sometimes be a sign of a more serious problem.
warnings: Tell your doctor if you have liver problems, kidney disease, or if you are pregnant or breastfeeding, as pitavastatin should not be used in these situations. Rarely, it can cause a serious muscle condition called rhabdomyolysis, which can damage the kidneys — seek medical attention right away if you have severe muscle pain, weakness, or dark-colored urine. Avoid drinking large amounts of grapefruit juice, as it may affect how this medication works.
typical_dosing: Pitavastatin is usually taken as one tablet by mouth once a day, at any time of day, with or without food. The typical starting dose is 2 mg per day, and your doctor may adjust it up to a maximum of 4 mg per day based on how your cholesterol responds. Try to take it at the same time each day to help you remember.
